## Purpose

Cross-cutting security and configuration primitives with no knowledge of any specific pipeline
or route: `Settings` (env-driven config, [config.py](../../backend/app/core/config.py)), JWT + password hashing ([security.py](../../backend/app/core/security.py)),
FastAPI auth dependencies ([dependencies.py](../../backend/app/core/dependencies.py)), at-rest secret encryption ([crypto.py](../../backend/app/core/crypto.py)), and
tier-based feature gating ([entitlements.py](../../backend/app/core/entitlements.py)).

**Nearly every other backend module depends on it transitively** — auth on every protected
route, `settings` read everywhere from model selection to shutdown timing.

## Shape

- [config.py](../../backend/app/core/config.py) — `Settings(BaseSettings)` (pydantic-settings), a single `settings` module-level
  instance read everywhere. Fields fall into bands: LLM provider selection (Anthropic direct /
  Bedrock IAM / Bedrock bearer-token / Mistral fallback), output/token/timeout ceilings
  (`MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, `LLM_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`), SSE transport tuning
  (`SSE_KEEPALIVE_PING_SECONDS`, `SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE`), graceful-shutdown budgets
  (`SHUTDOWN_CONCIERGE_DRAIN_SECONDS`, `SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS`), sandbox/runtime knobs
  (`RUNS_ROOT`, `AGENT_RECURSION_LIMIT`, `RUN_DIR_TTL_HOURS`), and auth/db basics
  (`SECRET_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS`).

  Two `@model_validator` hooks run at construction: `_default_shutdown_stop_runs_from_env`
  (env-differentiated default, only when unset) and `_validate_secret_key` (refuses to boot on
  a default/weak `SECRET_KEY` outside `ENV=development`, raising `SecretKeyMisconfigured`).
  `redact_db_url()` strips the inline Postgres password before any boot-banner logging.
- [security.py](../../backend/app/core/security.py) — `hash_password`/`verify_password` (bcrypt); `create_access_token`/
  `decode_access_token` (JWT, `HS256`, signed with `settings.SECRET_KEY`, each token minted
  with a fresh `jti`); `is_token_revoked(jti, db)` — the single revocation-lookup used by both
  the HTTP dependency and the WebSocket handler.
- [dependencies.py](../../backend/app/core/dependencies.py) — FastAPI `Depends()` chain for route auth: `get_current_user` /
  `get_current_user_with_payload` decode the bearer token, reject on per-`jti` revocation and
  on tokens issued before the user's last password change (`_check_password_change_revocation`,
  compared at whole-second `iat` resolution), and lazily GC expired revocation rows
  (~1-in-1000 requests). `get_user_for_logout` is a deliberately laxer variant that treats
  "already revoked" as success so `/logout` is idempotent.
- [crypto.py](../../backend/app/core/crypto.py) — `encrypt_pat`/`decrypt_pat`: Fernet symmetric encryption for GitHub PATs stored
  at rest, keyed by an HKDF-derived key from `settings.SECRET_KEY` (not the raw key, so a
  leaked JWT-signing key doesn't also decrypt stored PATs).
- [entitlements.py](../../backend/app/core/entitlements.py) — `TIER_PIPELINES` (which pipeline types each tier — basic/hexaware/pro/
  enterprise — may run), `UPGRADE_PATH`, and `can_run_pipeline(user_tier, pipeline_type)`.

## Why this shape

**Fail-closed by construction**: a missing/default `SECRET_KEY` refuses to boot outside dev
rather than silently signing JWTs with a known key, and PATs are encrypted with a key *derived
from* (not equal to) the signing secret so the two compromise scenarios are independent.
[crypto.py](../../backend/app/core/crypto.py) uses no per-record salt deliberately — the threat model is "DB-only compromise vs.
full secret leak," and a per-tenant salt would only add lookup complexity without changing
that boundary.

[dependencies.py](../../backend/app/core/dependencies.py) splits "strict" (`get_current_user`) from "idempotent-friendly"
(`get_user_for_logout`) rather than parameterizing one function, keeping each call site's
revocation semantics explicit instead of behind a flag.

[config.py](../../backend/app/core/config.py) centralizes every environment-differentiated runtime knob (shutdown budgets, SSE
tuning, sandbox TTLs) as a single `Settings` object rather than scattering `os.getenv()` calls
through the codebase, so `extra = "ignore"` is required (production's secrets-loader pours
every SSM key into the env, and boto3 reads its own `AWS_*` vars) but every value this app
actually reads is declared and typed.

This module deliberately excludes persistence models (delegated to `[MOD-backend-app-models](MOD-backend-app-models.md)`)
and route handlers (`[MOD-backend-app-api](MOD-backend-app-api.md)`) — it is pure cross-cutting policy.
